reader.title: Attempted lynching of Coffee in Aubry Valley
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: A1 says several men gathered 'for the purpose of lynching' Coffee, who escaped with his friends' help, so this is a threatened lynching; no race is given for anyone (A1).
A single reprinted item from the Miner (A1) is the only report found; no other paper or follow-up turned up.

summary.text: The attempted lynching of Coffee was a threatened mob killing in Arizona Territory in January 1882, when several men gathered at a saloon to lynch a man named Coffee who had just shot another man.
Coffee's friends got him away, and he later surrendered to a deputy sheriff at Murphy's Camp in Aubry Valley.
The episode is known from a single brief credited to the Miner, which gives no race for anyone involved.
The surviving text opens in the middle of the story, so the wounded man's name and the date and town of the shooting are lost.
According to the item, the man made an "allusion to Coffee's parentage" (the standard OCR reads "percentage"), and Coffee drew his revolver and shot him in the breast.
The ball passed through the left lung and lodged in the back, and Dr. Day, unable to find the bullet, said the man could not live.
Coffee then went to a saloon, printed "Fay's" or "Pays" in the two readings of the text, and within a few hours "several men commenced to gather around for the purpose of lynching him."
Through the efforts of his friends he got away before the men acted.
Deputy Sheriff Davis was notified and found Coffee and his friends, all armed, at Murphy's Camp in Aubry Valley.
The friends meant to "stand Davis off" so that Coffee could escape, but after considerable talking Coffee gave himself up.
He was taken to "the Park" on the Tuesday of that week.
No report of the wounded man's death, an examination, an indictment or a trial was found.
The Arizona Weekly Citizen reprinted the item on 29 January 1882, crediting it to the Miner.
It treated the gathering as routine local news, used no racial terms, and passed no judgment on the men who meant to lynch Coffee.
Its one comment was aimed at the accused: "Coffee has some money, and he will probably use it to good advantage, like some of the rest."
No other paper carrying the story was found.

accounts.label: Miner local item (reprinted)
accounts.gist: Coffee shot a man who had made an allusion to his parentage, went to a saloon where several men began gathering to lynch him, escaped with friends, and surrendered to a deputy sheriff at Murphy's Camp.

framing.detail: A plain news brief reprinted among Prescott-area notes, with no comment on the would-be lynchers and a closing jab that Coffee 'has some money' and would use it 'like some of the rest'.
